newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chips, bonds fall, dollar up on rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips, bonds fall, dollar up on rate hike fears.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks and bonds fell, but the dollar rose Thursday as strong economic reports bolstered prospects that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next week to keep inflation in check.

The Dow Jones industrial average closed 9.62 points lower at 5,867.74. In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,242 to 1,102 on active volume of 395 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq index was up 6.38 points at 1,212.09, nearing its record close of 1,249.15 set on June 5.
"It's a day where techs are up and the rest of the market is languishing," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross.
"A lot of the big-cap techs that have been strong are staying strong and the former high-flyers that were killed (in the July market correction) are coming back," he said.
The Nasdaq index, which is studded with high technology stocks, has surged 6 percent since the start of September, while the Dow Jones index has risen only 4 percent during the same period.

Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker, said some of the key technology stocks were benefitting from "window-dressing," or buying by portfolio managers to make their accounts look stronger at the end of the third quarter.

Interest-rate sensitive blue chip stocks, however, were hounded anew by worries that strong economic growth may provoke the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at next Tuesday's policy-setting meeting to ward off inflation.

Strong housing starts, lower-than-expected weekly jobless claims and a jump in the Philadelphia Federal Reserve's regional prices index for September lent more credence to expectations that the Fed may boost interest rates.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was off 12/32 raising its yield to 7.05 percent from 7.03 percent at Wednesday's close.
In late New York trading, the dollar stood at 1.5136 German marks, up from 1.5090 marks Wednesday. The dollar fetched 109.44 Japanese yen, up from 109.12 yen.
Gasoline prices ended sharply lower as talk of imports from Europe arriving on top of ample U.S. stocks fuelled concerns of oversupply.
Gasoline for October delivery settled down 1.74 cent at 61.32 cents a gallon on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) after falling as low as 60.40 cents during the day.
October crude oil settled off 35 cents to $23.54 a barrel and October heating oil settled 1.10 cent lower to 66.77 cents a gallon on profit-taking.
At the New York Cotton Exchange, cotton prices rose Thursday on news of an unexpected jump in exports this past week. The October contract closed 0.80 cent higher at 74.25 cents per pound.
At New York's Commodity Exchange, silver prices tumbled largely because wealthy technical traders sold based on chart trends rather than supply and demand news.
December silver ended down 15.8 cents at $4.940 an ounce, after sinking to an 18 month low of $4.925.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index pushed to a record high of 3,987.7 points before ending at 3,974.3 points, up 18.6 points. In Tokyo, the key Nikkei 225 average powered up 166.10 points to close at 21,322.85.
